Mariolatry
mair-ee-OL-uh-tree
noun (the undue veneration of Mary)
From “Mary” and the Greek latreia (worship, service rendered to God); the excessive veneration of the Virgin Mary that trespasses upon the honour due to God alone.

Biblical Definition

Mariolatry is the excessive veneration of the Virgin Mary that trespasses upon the worship due to God alone, the corruption by which the mother of the Lord has been exalted in Roman and Eastern practice to a place Scripture never gives her. The dictionary honours Mary truly: she was the favoured one chosen to bear the incarnate Son, blessed among women, a woman of faith and humility whose song magnifies the Lord. But Mary herself confessed her need of a Saviour—“my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour”—and so was a sinner saved by grace like all the redeemed. When a woman cried out blessing on the womb that bore Him, the Lord gently redirected the praise: “Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.” Mary's own last recorded words point men away from herself to her Son: “Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.” The dictionary names as corruption the accumulated Marian dogmas and devotions of Rome: her Immaculate Conception, her bodily Assumption, her titles as Queen of Heaven, Mediatrix, and Co-Redemptrix, the rosary's repeated prayers addressed to her, and the seeking of her intercession as though she shared the office of the one Mediator. These rob Christ of glory and break the commandment that forbids bowing down to any but God. The dictionary holds the line the Reformation drew: honour Mary as the blessed and believing mother of the Lord, a sinner saved like ourselves, while refusing every prayer, title, and devotion that gives to the creature the worship and mediation belonging to God and to Christ alone.

Webster 1828 Definition

The excessive veneration of the Virgin Mary trespassing on worship due to God alone; the dictionary honours Mary as the blessed, believing mother of the Lord—herself a sinner saved by grace (Luke 1:47)—while rejecting Rome's Marian dogmas and prayers.

MARIOLATRY, noun. [Mary + Greek latreia, worship.] The undue veneration of Mary that trespasses on the honour due to God.

Mary is truly honoured: blessed among women, the believing mother of the Lord.

Yet she confessed her need of a Saviour: “God my Saviour” (Luke 1:47).

The Lord redirected praise from her womb to obedience to God's word (Luke 11:28).

Rejected: her Immaculate Conception, Assumption, and titles as Mediatrix and Queen of Heaven.

Key Scripture

Lu 1:47 — "And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour."

Lu 11:28 — "But he said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it."

Joh 2:5 — "His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it."

Ex 20:5 — "Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me;"

Modern Corruption

Mariolatry is itself the corruption: it exalts the creature to a place Scripture never gives her—Mediatrix, Co-Redemptrix, Queen of Heaven—robbing Christ of glory and breaking the command against bowing to any but God.

expand to see more

Mariolatry is not a doctrine to be guarded against drift but the corruption itself, named plainly. Rome and the East have heaped upon the mother of the Lord titles and devotions that belong to God and to Christ alone: Mediatrix and Co-Redemptrix, Queen of Heaven, the object of prayer and the rosary, credited with an Immaculate Conception and a bodily Assumption Scripture never teaches. The dictionary names these as corruptions of the first and second commandments and as a robbery of the glory of the one Mediator. Mary herself rejoiced in God her Saviour and pointed all to her Son; she neither sought nor received the worship later ages gave her.

The dictionary's correction is not the dishonouring of Mary but the recovery of her true honour. She was indeed blessed among women, the favoured and believing handmaid of the Lord, and the church may rightly call her blessed as she foretold. But she was a sinner saved by grace, as her own song confesses, and the New Testament never directs a prayer to her, never names her a mediator, never bids the church seek her intercession. To honour Mary as Scripture honours her is to magnify the Saviour she magnified; to exalt her as Rome exalts her is to take from Christ the glory He will not share. Whatsoever He saith unto you, do it—her last word remains her best.

Hebrew Roots

From “Mary” and the Greek latreia (the worship and service due to God alone, as distinguished by Rome from dulia and hyperdulia); the dictionary holds that the Marian devotions cross into latreia.

expand to see more

Latreia, Greek, the worship and service due to God alone.

Dulia and hyperdulia, Rome's terms for veneration of saints and of Mary.

“Theotokos,” “God-bearer,” a true Christological title abused into Marian exaltation.

“Mediatrix” and “Co-Redemptrix,” titles that trespass on Christ's sole mediation.

Set against the first and second commandments and the one Mediator (1 Timothy 2:5).

Usage

"The teacher honoured Mary as the believing mother of the Lord while naming mariolatry as corruption."

"He showed that Mary called God her Saviour, confessing herself a sinner saved by grace."

"She prayed to God alone, refusing the rosary's prayers addressed to the creature."
